directive.gatingQuestion: Does IonQ's rapid Q2 2026 revenue/RPO growth conflict with early commercialization and acquisition effects, after the prior resolver separated Q2 organic performance from post-quarter SkyWater contribution?
directive.whyItMatters: The live queue repeats the same unresolved_material_contradiction after prior closure; continued exception research is justified only if new evidence changes attribution or the disposition.
directive.successCondition: Find materially new evidence that changes Q2 acquisition attribution or preserve the resolved disposition and stop repeated resolver looping.

finding: Primary-source recheck remains unchanged. IonQ reported $80.1M Q2 revenue (+287% YoY) and described strong organic growth; the quarter ended June 30. SkyWater closed July 31, and IonQ's August $280M-$290M full-year outlook explicitly excluded SkyWater. Its September $450M-$460M outlook explicitly includes SkyWater beginning July 31. Therefore SkyWater does not explain reported Q2 revenue; fault-tolerant economics remain a separate uncertainty, not a factual contradiction with current commercial traction. Prior resolver evidence already resolved this exact route, so further resolver looping is unavailable as a productive closure path.

evidenceVsInference.evidence: IonQ reported $80.1M Q2 revenue (+287% YoY), stated strong organic growth, said the August FY2026 outlook excluded SkyWater, and later said September guidance includes SkyWater from July 31 onward.
evidenceVsInference.inference: Commercial traction and unproven fault-tolerant economics can coexist; acquisition-adjusted comparability remains an underwriting risk without sustaining the contradiction gate.

recommendedDisposition: Do not route IONQ back to deep-resolver for this unchanged contradiction. Reconcile prior closure; retain fault-tolerant economics, yield and acquisition-adjusted comparability as underwriting unknowns/risks.
